fields.Participants: Procurement Director, Category Managers (links to VS-01), Supply Planning (links to VS-02), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Treasury (links to VS-18)
fields.Trigger: Annual commodity-risk review; category strategy refresh

workflows.name: Commodity Exposure Mapping by SKU / Category / Vendor

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-import of "import-vs-local sourcing split" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "validate the exposure map against the merchandise plan" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-547 (ensure controlled execution — Commodity Exposure Identification & Market Intelligence (PA-106.1).)
- operational: quarterly refresh and vendor transparency (W3405); operational: landed-cost analysis (W3408)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mapping-staleness risk**: Outdated exposure map masks new risks (e.g., a vendor switches input source); mitigated by quarterly refresh and vendor transparency (W3405)
- **Hidden-exposure risk**: Indirect commodity content (e.g., oil-derived packaging/transport) understates true exposure; mitigated by landed-cost analysis (W3408)
System Touchpoints: - Item/vendor master (links to VS-29/W287); spend analytics (links to VS-67/VS-28.1); merchandise plan (links to VS-101); import pipeline (links to VS-02.2)

steps.activity: Procurement/Category Managers map each category's commodity exposure: identify the dominant input commodities (steel/rebar/cement/lumber for building materials; copper for electrical/plumbing; titanium dioxide/resins/solvents for paint; oil-derived plastics for tools/appliances), the exposure weight (% of COGS tied to each commodity), and the import-vs-local sourcing split (links to VS-02.2/VS-87)

Procurement tag SKUs and vendors with commodity exposure attributes in the item/vendor master (links to VS-29/W287), compute commodity-weighted spend by vendor/category/quarter using actuals, and rank the top commodity exposures by PHP impact (e.g., steel, copper, cement, lumber, resins, plastics)

Procurement/Treasury validate the exposure map against the merchandise plan (links to VS-101) and import pipeline (links to VS-02.2), publish the commodity-exposure heatmap, and feed it to sensitivity analysis (W3404) and mitigation planning (PA-106.2)

fields.Participants: Category Manager, Procurement, Vendor (links to VS-03.3/VS-41), Finance (links to VS-17.4/VS-85)
fields.Trigger: Exposure mapping (W3401); vendor cost-transparency initiative; private-label (links to VS-41)
fields.Volume: Top ~200–500 commodity-intensive SKUs (A-items per profile §6.6 ABC)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-measure of "measure per component" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "validate the BOM against vendor quotes and landed cost" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-547 (ensure controlled execution — Commodity Exposure Identification & Market Intelligence (PA-106.1).)
- operational: strategic/private-label leverage and open-book clauses (links to VS-41/VS-03); operational: vendor validation and periodic re-baselining
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor-resistance risk**: Vendors withhold cost transparency; mitigated by strategic/private-label leverage and open-book clauses (links to VS-41/VS-03.3)
- **Decomposition-error risk**: Wrong commodity weights distort sensitivity; mitigated by vendor validation and periodic re-baselining
System Touchpoints: - Product costing (links to VS-85/W85); private-label (links to VS-41); vendor contract (links to VS-03.3); merchandise analytics (links to VS-101.3)

steps.activity: Category Managers/Procurement build a BOM/input-cost decomposition for commodity-intensive SKUs (esp. private-label per VS-41): break the unit cost into raw-material commodity components (e.g., a power drill = motor copper + steel + plastic housing + battery + labor/overhead), with commodity weight and unit-of-measure per component

Category Managers/Vendor obtain vendor cost-transparency (open-book costing for strategic/private-label vendors per VS-03.3/VS-41), validate the BOM against vendor quotes and landed cost (links to VS-02.2/VS-87), and identify cost-driver concentration and negotiable vs fixed components

Finance/Category Managers load the decomposition into cost/margin analytics (links to VS-85/W85, VS-101.3), compute commodity-cost elasticity (how unit cost moves with commodity index), and feed to sensitivity (W3404) and indexed-pricing design (W3412)

fields.Participants: Procurement, Treasury (links to VS-18), Category Managers (links to VS-01), BI (links to VS-28.1)

workflows.name: Commodity Market-Price Intelligence & Benchmark Data Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "BI/Procurement integrate commodity-benchmark data into the analytics platform" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-detect of "detect over-pricing or lagging pass-through" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-547 (ensure controlled execution — Commodity Exposure Identification & Market Intelligence (PA-106.1).)
- operational: careful index selection and normalization; operational: multi-source cross-check and quality monitoring
Pain Points / Risks: - **Benchmark-mismatch risk**: Wrong grade/region index distorts comparison; mitigated by careful index selection and normalization
- **Data-reliability risk**: Poor-quality feeds drive wrong decisions; mitigated by multi-source cross-check and quality monitoring
System Touchpoints: - Market-data feeds; BI/analytics (links to VS-28.1); landed cost (links to VS-02.2/VS-87); FX master (links to VS-18.3/W307)

steps.activity: Procurement/Treasury define the commodity benchmark set: LME steel/copper/nickel/aluminum, regional cement/clinker index, lumber/timber index, oil/brent (for plastics/solvents/transport), titanium dioxide/resin indices, and the PHP/USD and PHP/CNY rates (links to VS-18.3/W307); source data feeds (subscriptions, vendor indices, exchange data)

BI/Procurement integrate commodity-benchmark data into the analytics platform (links to VS-28.1), maintain history and seasonality, normalize units/currency, and compute price-change metrics (MoM, YoY, vs moving average); quality-check feeds

Procurement/Category Managers benchmark vendor-quoted prices and landed costs (links to VS-02.2/VS-87/W239) against market indices to detect over-pricing or lagging pass-through; feed deviations to vendor negotiation (links to VS-03.3) and pass-through governance (W3417)

fields.Participants: Treasury Manager, Procurement, FP&A (links to VS-17.4), Risk (links to VS-21.2)
fields.Trigger: Monthly risk review; exposure map update (W3401)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-reconcile of "reconcile to the ERM risk register" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report, set the hedge/mitigation priority" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-70 (ensure commodity exposure & hedge accounting accuracy.)
- operational: validation and back-testing; operational: granular decomposition
Pain Points / Risks: - **Model-risk**: Wrong sensitivity/VaR assumptions mis-state exposure; mitigated by validation and back-testing
- **Concentration-blindspot risk**: Aggregate VaR masks single-vendor/single-category concentration; mitigated by granular decomposition
System Touchpoints: - Risk/analytics platform (links to VS-28.1/VS-21.2); FP&A (links to VS-17.4); merchandise plan (links to VS-101); ERM (links to VS-21.2)

steps.activity: Treasury/Procurement compute commodity sensitivity: for each top commodity, the PHP impact of a ±5/10/20% price move on the forward purchase plan (links to VS-02.1/VS-101 receipt plan), using the BOM decomposition (W3402) and exposure map (W3401); produce a sensitivity matrix

Treasury/Risk measure commodity Value-at-Risk (VaR) and stress scenarios: probability-weighted exposure over the planning horizon, stress tests (e.g., +30% steel, oil shock, supply disruption links to VS-69/VS-02.3), and the combined commodity+FX impact (W3408); reconcile to the ERM risk register (links to VS-21.2)

Treasury/Procurement publish the commodity-exposure and VaR report, set the hedge/mitigation priority (links to PA-106.2), and report to the commodity-risk governance (W3406) and FP&A margin plan (links to VS-101.3/VS-17.4)

fields.Participants: Procurement Director, Category Managers, Vendor (links to VS-03.3/VS-03.4), Legal (links to VS-100.3)
fields.Trigger: Strategic-vendor review; contract renewal (links to VS-03.3)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "document each strategic vendor's cost-structure transparency" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review/insert contract clauses governing commodity pass-through" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor actual pass-through behavior vs clause" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-547 (ensure controlled execution — Commodity Exposure Identification & Market Intelligence (PA-106.1).)
- operational: open-book clauses and index benchmarking (W3403); operational: Legal review (links to VS-100)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Opacity risk**: Vendors hide commodity savings and pass through increases only; mitigated by open-book clauses and index benchmarking (W3403)
- **Clause-enforceability risk**: Vague/index-less clauses are unenforceable; mitigated by Legal review (links to VS-100.3)
System Touchpoints: - Vendor contract (links to VS-03.3/W230/W402); supplier portal (links to VS-03.4); vendor master (links to W287); legal matter (links to VS-100.3)

steps.activity: Category Managers/Procurement obtain and document each strategic vendor's cost-structure transparency: input-commodity composition (W3402), pricing formula/frequency, index reference, pass-through mechanism (raw-material surcharge, formula price, periodic renegotiation), and lag/lead vs market (W3403)

Procurement/Legal review/insert contract clauses governing commodity pass-through (raw-material adjustment formula, index, frequency, cap/floor, notice, audit right), indexing mechanics, and duration; ensure clauses are enforceable and benchmarked to market (links to VS-100.3/W230)

Procurement maintain the vendor cost-transparency register (vendor, clause type, index, lag, exposure), monitor actual pass-through behavior vs clause (W3417), and feed insights to vendor negotiation (links to VS-03.3) and mitigation strategy (PA-106.2)

fields.Participants: CFO, Procurement Director, Treasury Manager, Risk (links to VS-21.2), Internal Audit (links to VS-21)
fields.Trigger: Annual risk framework review (links to VS-21.2); board governance cycle (links to VS-36)

workflows.name: Commodity Risk Register, Appetite & Governance Framework

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "enterprise risk register" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review commodity-risk controls and policy adherence" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-70 (ensure commodity exposure & hedge accounting accuracy.)
- operational: clear policy and authority matrix; operational: quarterly refresh
Pain Points / Risks: - **Appetite-misalignment risk**: Hedging activity exceeds/misaligns with board appetite; mitigated by clear policy and authority matrix
- **Register-staleness risk**: Outdated register masks emerging risk; mitigated by quarterly refresh
System Touchpoints: - ERM/risk register (links to VS-21.2); policy repository (links to VS-186); audit (links to VS-21); board reporting (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Treasury/Risk maintain the commodity risk register: each commodity exposure (W3401), sensitivity/VaR (W3404), vendor/clause status (W3405), current mitigation (PA-106.2), residual risk, owner, and trend; integrate to the enterprise risk register (links to VS-21.2/W122)

CFO/exec committee set the commodity-risk appetite and policy: acceptable margin-at-risk, hedge ratio guidelines, use of financial vs physical hedges, indexed-contract limits, strategic-inventory limits (links to VS-101 OTB), and authority matrix for hedging/pass-through decisions

Internal Audit/CFO review commodity-risk controls and policy adherence (links to VS-21), report to the Audit Committee/Board (links to VS-36), and approve framework updates; ensure disclosure of material commodity risk in financial reporting (links to VS-17)

fields.Participants: Procurement, Treasury, Category Managers (links to VS-01), Merchandising (links to VS-101), FP&A

workflows.name: Market Outlook, Forecast & Commodity Intelligence Briefing

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-compile of "compile the weekly commodity flash" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-post of "posture, and implications for OTB/receipts" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document decisions for governance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-547 (ensure controlled execution — Commodity Exposure Identification & Market Intelligence (PA-106.1).)
- operational: scenario ranges and humility bias; operational: weekly flash and event triggers
Pain Points / Risks: - **Forecast-error risk**: Wrong outlook drives over/under-buy or wrong hedge; mitigated by scenario ranges and humility bias
- **Latency risk**: Late briefings miss the decision window; mitigated by weekly flash and event triggers
System Touchpoints: - Market data/BI (links to VS-28.1/W3403); merchandise plan (links to VS-101); price management (links to VS-01.2); risk register (links to VS-21.2)

steps.activity: Procurement/Treasury compile the weekly commodity flash: price movement on tracked commodities/indices (W3403), key drivers (supply, demand, geopolitics, FX links to VS-18.3), BuildRight exposure impact (W3404), and any vendor/market signal (e.g., cement allocation, steel quota, shipping freight)

Procurement/Category Managers publish the monthly commodity intelligence briefing: outlook/forecast per commodity, scenario views, recommended buying/timing/hedging posture, and implications for OTB/receipts (links to VS-101 W3283/W3284) and pricing (links to VS-01.2/W3417); brief Merchandising and FP&A

Procurement/Treasury convene ad-hoc briefings on market shocks (oil spike, steel quota, typhoon supply disruption links to VS-69) and trigger the rapid-response mitigation (links to PA-106.2/W3418) and price-action (links to VS-01.2/W329) workflow; document decisions for governance (W3406)

fields.Participants: Treasury Manager, Import/Procurement (links to VS-02.2/VS-87), FP&A, Logistics Finance (links to VS-17)
fields.Trigger: Import buy planning (links to VS-02.2); monthly exposure review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-import of "Import decompose the import landed cost into commodity + FX + freight/duty +…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-measure of "measure the interaction/correlation between commodity price, FX" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate the FX hedge" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-547 (ensure controlled execution — Commodity Exposure Identification & Market Intelligence (PA-106.1).)
- operational: integrated landed-cost analysis; operational: landed-cost decomposition
Pain Points / Risks: - **Double-count/miss risk**: Hedging commodity and FX separately without interaction view can double-hedge or leave a gap; mitigated by integrated landed-cost analysis
- **Freight-blindspot risk**: Ignoring freight volatility understates import exposure; mitigated by landed-cost decomposition
System Touchpoints: - Landed-cost (links to VS-02.2 W2B.12); FX (links to VS-18.3/W307); freight (links to VS-06/VS-87); margin analytics (links to VS-101.3)

steps.activity: Treasury/Import decompose the import landed cost into commodity + FX + freight/duty + handling components (links to VS-02.2 W2B.12 landed cost, VS-87 duty, VS-18.3 FX), and quantify each component's share and volatility for top import commodities (steel, copper, tiles, paint raws, tools)

Treasury measure the interaction/correlation between commodity price, FX (PHP/USD, PHP/CNY), and freight (per VS-06/VS-87), and the combined landed-cost sensitivity (e.g., steel up 10% + PHP weakens 5% + freight up 20%); isolate hedgeable vs unhedgeable components

Treasury/Import publish the integrated landed-cost exposure view, coordinate the FX hedge (links to VS-18.3/W80/W321) with the commodity hedge (PA-106.2), and feed the combined exposure to margin/price decisions (links to VS-101.3/VS-01.2) and the merchandise plan (links to VS-101)
